questions.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-3y+z=-1 \\ x-y+3z=2 \\ -2x+y-z=1\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, and the inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & -8 \\ -5 & 0 & -5 \\ -1 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

the solution of the system of equations is 

$x=$
{{field-1}}, 
$\,y=$
{{field-2}}, 
$\,z=$
{{field-3}}.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & -8 \\ -5 & 0 & -5 \\ -1 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ 0 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is 

$$
x=-1,\,y=0,\,z=1.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2y+4z=-2 \\ x+3y+9z=0 \\ y+6z=3\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*

$$
\,{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}9 & -8 & 6 \\ -6 & 6 & -5 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -8 & 6 \\ -6 & 6 & -5 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is $x=0,y=-3,z=1.$

Finally, $x+y+z=0+(-3)+1=-2.$

$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$

$$
\,{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -1 \\ -13 & -15 & -11 \\ 18 & 22 & 16\end{aligned}].

questions.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 \\ 5 & 1 & 1 \\ -8 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}4x-3y+2z=-4 \\ -4x+4y-3z=7 \\ x-y+z=-2\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*

$$
\,{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}4 & -3 & 2 \\ -4 & 4 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 7 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 7 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is $x=1,y=2,z=-1.$

Finally, $x+y+z=1+2+(-1)=2.$

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+3z=2 \\ x-2y-5z=-1 \\ 2x-3y+2z=1\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*

$$
\,{A}^{-1}=-\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}-19 & -7 & 11 \\ -12 & -4 & 8 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 \\ 1 & -2 & -5 \\ 2 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}-19 & -7 & 11 \\ -12 & -4 & 8 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
{\begin{aligned}z+x=2 \\ 2y-3z=1 \\ 2z-y=-3x+3\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We organize the system so that it’s in the correct order first:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x+z=2 \\ 2y-3z=1 \\ 3x-y+2z=3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1|\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|-0|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(4-3)-0+(0-6) \\  & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 9 & -6 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}1 & -9 & -6 \\ -1 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 \\ -9 & -1 & 3 \\ -6 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=-\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 \\ -9 & -1 & 3 \\ -6 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 \\ -9 & -1 & 3 \\ -6 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence the solution is $x=1,y=2,z=1.$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-3+z=0 \\ 5y-1+3x=2z+1 \\ 3z+2x-1=2y\end{aligned}
$$

Find  $x+y+z.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the system in the correct order:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+z=3 \\ 3x+5y-2z=2 \\ 2x-2y+3z=1\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we  write the system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & 5 & -2 \\ 2 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & 5 & -2 \\ 2 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}|-0+|\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(15-4)+(-6-10) \\  & =22-16 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

 

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}11 & 13 & -16 \\ 2 & 4 & -4 \\ -5 & -7 & 10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}11 & -13 & -16 \\ -2 & 4 & 4 \\ -5 & 7 & 10\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}11 & -2 & -5 \\ -13 & 4 & 7 \\ -16 & 4 & 10\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}11 & -2 & -5 \\ -13 & 4 & 7 \\ -16 & 4 & 10\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the solution to the given system is

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}11 & -2 & -5 \\ -13 & 4 & 7 \\ -16 & 4 & 10\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}24 \\ -24 \\ -30\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4 \\ -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $x+y+z=4-4-5=-5.$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2y+3z+x=-1 \\ 4z+y=1 \\ 5x+6y-3=-3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We organize the system so that it’s in the correct order first:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x+2y+3z=-1 \\ y+4z=1 \\ 5x+6y=0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 5 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 5 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}|-2|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}|+3|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 5 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(-24)-2(-20)+3(-5) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 5 & 6\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 5 & 6\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-24 & -20 & -5 \\ -18 & -15 & -4 \\ 5 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-24 & 20 & -5 \\ 18 & -15 & 4 \\ 5 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-24 & 18 & 5 \\ 20 & -15 & -4 \\ -5 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=\frac{1}{1}[\begin{aligned}-24 & 18 & 5 \\ 20 & -15 & -4 \\ -5 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-24 & 18 & 5 \\ 20 & -15 & -4 \\ -5 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}42 \\ -35 \\ 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence the solution is $x=42,y=-35,z=9.$

questions.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+z=4x+y+2 \\ x+y=2z+2 \\ y=x-y+z+1\end{aligned}
$$

Find the solution $x=[x,y,z]^{T}$ of the system by computing the inverse of the coefficient matrix.

|  |  | {{field-1}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x=\,\,$ |  | {{field-2}} |  |
|  |  | {{field-3}} |  |
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the system in the correct order:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3x-y+z=2 \\ x+y-2z=2 \\ -x+2y-z=1\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we  write the system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}|-(-1)|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3(-1+4)+(-1-2)+(2+1) \\  & =-9-3+3 \\  & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -3 & 3 \\ -1 & 4 & -7 \\ 1 & 5 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 & 7 \\ 1 & -5 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & -5 \\ 3 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=-\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & -5 \\ 3 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the solution to the given system is

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & -5 \\ 3 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 9 \\ 18\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x+3y+z=6 \\ 4x+7y+2z=0 \\ 3x+y+z=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 1 \\ 4 & 7 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 1 \\ 4 & 7 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}7 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|-3|\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}4 & 7 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(7-2)-3(-2)+1(4-21) \\  & =10+6-17 \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}7 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}4 & 7 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 7 & 2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 4 & 7\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & -17 \\ 2 & -1 & -7 \\ -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -17 \\ -2 & -1 & 7 \\ -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ -17 & 7 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=-\frac{1}{1}[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ -17 & 7 & 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 17 & -7 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 17 & -7 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-29 \\ -12 \\ 100\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence the solution is $x=-29,y=-12,z=100.$

questions.problem:
Consider a system of $n$ linear equations in $n$ variables, written in matrix form as $D\,z=c.$ Here, $D$ is the non-singular coefficient matrix of the system, $z$ is the column vector containing the variables, and $c$ is the column vector containing the constants. The unique solution of the system can be found using the method shown below:

$$
\begin{aligned}D\,z & =c \\ {D}^{-1}D\,z & =c \\ z & ={D}^{-1}\,c \\ z & ={D}^{-1}\,c\end{aligned}
$$

From top to bottom and right to left, what are the missing parts of the derivation?
questions.worked_solution:
Since $D$ is not singular, it must have an inverse ${D}^{-1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $D\,z=c$ by ${D}^{-1},$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}D\,z & =c \\ {D}^{-1}D\,z & ={D}^{-1}c \\ {I}_{n}\,z & ={D}^{-1}\,c \\ z & ={D}^{-1}\,c\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing parts are ${D}^{-1}$ and ${I}_{n}.$

questions.problem:
Consider a system of $3$ linear equations in $3$ variables, written in matrix form as $D\,y=w.$ Here, $D$ is the non-singular coefficient matrix of the system, $y$ is the column vector containing the variables, and $w$ is the column vector containing the constants. The unique solution of the system can be found using the method shown below:

$$
\begin{aligned}D\,y & =w \\ {D}^{-1}D\,y & =w \\ {I}_{3}\,y & ={D}^{-1}\,w \\  & ={D}^{-1}\,w\end{aligned}
$$

From top to bottom and left to right, what are the missing parts of the derivation?
questions.worked_solution:
Since $D$ is not singular, it must have an inverse ${D}^{-1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $D\,y=w$ by ${D}^{-1},$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}D\,y & =w \\ {D}^{-1}D\,y & ={D}^{-1}w \\ {I}_{3}\,y & ={D}^{-1}\,w \\ y & ={D}^{-1}\,w\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing parts are ${D}^{-1}$ and $y.$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Given the Inverse of the Coefficient Matrix
canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2x+5y-2z=-2 \\ -3y+z=-2 \\ 3x-7y+3z=3\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}.$ Given that $\mathbf x = \langle x,y,z\rangle$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 & -1 \\ 3 & 0 & 2 \\ 9 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, let's write our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 3 & -7 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the solution to $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ is given by $\mathbf{x}= A^{-1}\mathbf{b}.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 & -1 \\ 3 & 0 & 2 \\ 9 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is $x=3, y=0, z=-2.$

Finally, $x+y+z=3+0+(-2)=1.$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations By Calculating the Inverse of the Coefficient Matrix
canonical_examples.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations using matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}3y+x+z=0 \\ z+4y-5=2 \\ 1+2x-y=-3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we organize the system so that the variables are in the correct order and every variable has a coefficient:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x+3y+z=0 \\ 0x+4y+z=7 \\ 2x-y+0z=-4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we  write the system in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, the solution to $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ is given by $\mathbf{x}= A^{-1}\mathbf{b}.$ So, we compute $A^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1*: Find the determinant of $A.$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A)=|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| & =1|\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|-3|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(1)-3(-2)+(-8) \\  & =1+6-8 \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2*: Compute the matrix of minors.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -8 \\ 1 & -2 & -7 \\ -1 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3*:  Find the matrix of cofactors.

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -8 \\ -1 & -2 & 7 \\ -1 & -1 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

*Step 4*: Transpose the matrix of cofactors.

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & -2 & -1 \\ -8 & 7 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

*Step 5*: Apply the inverse matrix formula.

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & -2 & -1 \\ -8 & 7 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, we can calculate the solution as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 2 & 1 \\ 8 & -7 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 10 \\ -33\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=3,$ $y=10,$ $z=-33.$

canonical_examples.problem: Consider a matrix equation $B\,\mathbf{x} = A^{-1}\,\mathbf{d},$ where $A$ and $B$ are $10 \times 10$ non-singular matrices, while $\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathbf{d}$ are $10 \times 1$ column vectors. Solve the equation for $\mathbf{x}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Since $B$ is not singular, it must have an inverse $B^{−1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $B\,\mathbf{x} = A^{-1}\,\mathbf{d}$ by $B^{-1},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}B\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,d \\ {B}^{-1}B\,x & ={B}^{-1}{A}^{-1}\,d \\ {I}_{10}\,x & ={B}^{-1}{A}^{-1}\,d \\ x & ={B}^{-1}{A}^{-1}\,d.\end{aligned}
$$
